macros.name: defineletterhead
macros.doc: The \defineletterhead macro takes two arguments: the first is the name of the letterhead, the second is the letterhead code itself.

macros.name: yaaddress
macros.doc: \yaaddress just typesets the address, and doesn’t set any other variables.

macros.name: yadate
macros.doc: \yadate takes a single argument, which is the date that you want to be printed.

macros.name: yadatestyle
macros.doc: You can style your date arbitrarily by putting your style commands into the macro \yadatestyle.

macros.name: yaenclosure
macros.doc: The enclosure is included by issuing \yaenclosure.

macros.name: yaenvelope
macros.doc: \yaenvelope takes two arguments, the width and height of the envelope.

macros.name: yafarewell
macros.doc: Insert the farewell with \yafarewell, which is indented from the left margin by the value of \yahfarewellskip.

macros.name: yafromaddress
macros.doc: \yafromaddress sets the writer but does not typeset the address.

macros.name: yahsalutationskip
macros.doc: The salutation will be indented from the left by the distance \yahsalutationskip, which can be set in either the plain TeX or LaTeX ways.

macros.name: yahsignatureskip
macros.doc: The signature is indented by the value of \yahsignatureskip, which can be set in the usual ways.

macros.name: yainsideaddr
macros.doc: The macro \yainsideaddr takes a single argument, which is the inside address you want to be typeset.

macros.name: yainsideaddrstyle
macros.doc: You can insert style commands for your inside address using the \yainsideaddrstyle macro, which takes one argument, which is the style commands you desire.

macros.name: yalabelmarg
macros.doc: You can indent the box from the left edge of the label by setting the length \yalabelmarg, which defaults to 0.1in.

macros.name: yalabelsheet

arg.snippet: yalabelsheet{${1:page width}}{${2:page height}}{${3:label width}}{${4:label height}}{${5:horizontal separation}}{${6:vertical separation}}{${7:number across}}{${8:number down}}

macros.doc: \yalabelsheet, which takes eight arguments: the width and height of the page itself, the width and height of each label, the vertical and horizontal distance between each label, how many labels are across the width of the page, and how many labels are down the height of the page.

macros.name: yalabeltext
macros.doc: Redefining \yalabeltext will place the contents of that macro in each of the labels on the newly-created label page.

macros.name: yaletterblock
macros.doc: To explicitly request block format, issue \yaletterblock in your preamble.

macros.name: yaletternormal
macros.doc: To get normal format, issue \yaletternormal in your preamble.

macros.name: yaoptions
macros.doc: yaletter has the command \yaoptions, which gives the user the ability to set a variety of different dimensions within the letter.

macros.name: yaparindent
macros.doc: The actual indentation for paragraphs is governed by the special length \yaparindent.

macros.name: yaparskip
macros.doc: The actual space between paragraphs is governed by the special length \yaparskip.

macros.name: yasalutation
macros.doc: The salutation, typically just “Dear So-and-so,” is produced by the command \yasalutation.

macros.name: yatoaddress
macros.doc: The \yatoaddress macro both typesets the address itself and resets \yaaddressee to the short name given in \defineaddress.

macros.name: yauseletterhead
macros.doc: You can also use a letterhead via the \yauseletterhead command, which takes a single argument: the name assigned to the letterhead in the \defineletterhead command.
